character.name: Pip Tunnelly
character.background: A young hobbit of Bywater who reads the weather better than books, and talks his way out of most trouble.

scenes.title: The Garden Gate
scenes.text: Morning mist lies over Bywater. Old Mother Burrows hammers on your gate: her grandson's silver acorn, an heirloom, was snatched in the night, and muddy boot prints lead off toward the river. The sky to the west looks heavy.

choices.text: Walk down the lane to the Green Dragon
Read the clouds before you go (Weather-lore)

scenes.title: The Green Dragon
scenes.text: The inn is warm and loud. In the corner a tall stranger in a wet cloak keeps his hand on a bulging pocket and watches the door.

choices.text: Spin him a tale and look in his pocket (Hobbit Chatter -1)
Follow him when he slips out

scenes.title: Bagshot Hill
scenes.text: You climb the hill and see the storm coming. From up here you also see the path the thief took: across Farmer Cotton's fields, toward the ferry.

choices.text: Take the short way through the fields

scenes.title: Farmer Cotton's Fields
scenes.text: Tall barley hides you. Ahead, by the hedge, something grey and lean is sniffing the thief's trail.

choices.text: Creep past it through the barley (Hobbit Quietness)

scenes.title: Teeth in the Hedge
scenes.text: A grey wolf, far from the wild, bursts out of the hedge with a snarl.

scenes.title: The Brandywine Bank
scenes.text: The river runs fast and brown after the night's rain. On the far bank the stranger is loading a little boat.

choices.text: Swim across before he casts off (Swimming -2)

scenes.title: Ending: Home by Supper
scenes.text: You haul yourself out of the water right beside the boat. The stranger is so startled that he drops the silver acorn and flees. You are back in Bywater in time for supper, and Mother Burrows bakes you a seed cake.

scenes.title: The Ferry
scenes.text: At the ferry the stranger turns and draws a long knife. "Go home, little one," he says.

scenes.title: Ending: The Acorn Returned
scenes.text: The ruffian goes into the river and comes up far downstream, with no acorn and no pride. The Shirriffs hear the tale by evening, and your name is toasted at the Green Dragon for a week.
